contracts.commit_point: multi_user_share_access.py:25 — `task_id = cls._share.new_task(category, task_content)` executed inside MultiUserShareAccess.add_task under the asyncio Condition (lines 24-26, followed by notify_all), reached from the guarded call at tools.py:27.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Closure-captured allowlist in the tool factory: TaskShareToolFactory.build_new_task_tool(allowed_categories) (tools.py:15) builds an @tool-decorated async add_new_task whose first body statement is the guard `if category not in allowed_categories: return "Invalid category. Only categories {allowed_categories} are allowed."` (tools.py:24-25), returning before `await MultiUserShareAccess.add_task(category, content)` (tools.py:27). Each agent module supplies its own module-level allowlist: supervisor.py:5 defines [Category.INFRASTRUCTURE, Category.APPLICATION] and passes it via _get_add_new_task_tool (supervisor.py:11-12); user_agent.py:5 defines [Category.SUPERVISOR] and passes it via _get_add_new_task_tool (user_agent.py:12-13).
contracts.forbidden_condition: An add_new_task tool invocation whose category argument is not a member of the registering agent's allowed_categories list reaching the enqueue path — i.e., `category not in allowed_categories` evaluating true at tools.py:24 without the early return, allowing the call at tools.py:27 to commit a task into a category outside the registering agent's tier.

contracts.protected_operation: Adding a new task to the shared task queue via MultiUserShareAccess.add_task(category, content), invoked from the per-agent add_new_task tool.
contracts.protected_resource: The shared in-memory task queue held by MultiUserShareAccess._share (TaskShare), scoped per Category (multi_user_share_access.py:10-17, 21-35).
contracts.protection_obligation: Each agent's add_new_task tool must reject any requested task category not present in the _ALLOWED_CATEGORIES list registered at tool construction, before the task is committed to the shared TaskShare, so that per-tier task targeting is enforced: the user-facing agent (UserAgent, allowed=[Category.SUPERVISOR]) cannot enqueue tasks directly to infrastructure/application workers, and the SupervisorAgent (allowed=[Category.INFRASTRUCTURE, Category.APPLICATION]) cannot enqueue tasks into the SUPERVISOR category (i.e., to the user tier or itself). (Merges the two reviewer wordings, which describe the same allowlist guard, commit point, and per-agent registrations.)
scope_limits: The allowlist is enforced only inside the add_new_task tool wrapper; MultiUserShareAccess.add_task itself performs no category authorization, so any caller path that bypasses the tool would not be guarded (no such path is visible in the supplied views, but the module set is not complete).
Only the category parameter is checked; task content is unconstrained by this guard, and no content validation obligation is asserted here.

Allowlists are fixed at module definition/registration time; the guard does not validate Category enum membership or coerce the docstring-described integer codes (1/2/3) — category.py is not supplied.
Prompt-level task-routing constraints in the agent system prompts (supervisor.py:23-65, user_agent.py:24-40) are not code-enforced and are excluded from this contract.
